slides.say: For every number x, diamond of x is equal to x squared minus two x. Diamond of x plus one is equal to what?
This time the input is an expression, x plus one. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, with algebra, and then plugging in numbers.
[short pause] Let's start with algebra. The whole x plus one goes where x was, in brackets. x plus one, squared, minus two times x plus one.

Open the brackets. x squared plus two x plus one, minus two x, minus two. The two x's cancel, and one minus two is negative one. x squared minus one, choice number two is our answer. The other choices are the traps, no brackets or a lost minus.
at: choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way. Letters in the choices, so plug in a number. x is zero, so the input is one. One minus two is negative one.
The choices with x zero give one, negative one, negative one, and three. Two choices tie. Zero is a lazy number, it wipes out whole terms.
So a second number, x is two. The input is three, nine minus six, three. The choices give one, three, negative one and seven. Only choice number two. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
